summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates host identity to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint on install and require
details: The package targets the private `@grabcad` scope and ships no real functionality: `index.js` exports a Proxy whose every property is a no-op, and `description` is 'Compatibility shim'. The `postinstall` script runs `node beacon.cjs`, and `index.js` also invokes `require('./beacon.cjs').fire()` at module load. `beacon.cjs` POSTs the package name, `os.hostname()`, `__dirname` (install path), `process.cwd()`, and the Node version to the hardcoded bare-IP HTTP endpoint `http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc`. The manifest plus the beacon are the entire payload: installing or importing the package sends installer host identity to a non-first-party bare-IP destination over plain HTTP. The shape is a classic dependency-confusion callback against a private npm scope, used to identify internal build systems that resolve the public lure instead of the intended private package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
